reviews.text:
A terrible experience, to say the least.
I brought my cat with an acute ear infection that the owner said could be cured with a little iodine.
I was sent away with a 20ml bottle of iodine transferred from a 3-liter container at an additional cost of €6, plus the consultation fee.
The treatment was obviously ridiculous and useless, and after his condition worsened further, I was forced to take him to another clinic where he underwent intensive care.
Should we also add that he wouldn't give me a receipt after paying in cash?
Thanks, but never again!!!
EDIT TO THE RESPONSE RECEIVED:
1. THERE WAS ABSOLUTELY NO CYTOLOGICAL TEST. I WAS PRESENT DURING THE VISIT AND LEFT AFTER HALF AN HOUR.
2. THERE WAS NO ASSUMPTIONS ON MY PART EXCEPT FOR THE CONFIRMATION OF THE SECOND VETERINARY CLINIC REGARDING THE URGENT NEED FOR COMPREHENSIVE THERAPY DUE TO THE SEVERITY OF THE INFECTION.
THE IODINE TINCTURE SHE SUGGESTED WAS EMBARRASSING.
3. I NEVER ASKED FOR ANY DISCOUNT OF ANY KIND, AS MY CAT'S WELL-BEING IS MY PRIORITY. I PAID EVERYTHING IN CASH WITHOUT RECEIPT OR INVOICE.

Absolutely to be avoided from all points of view.
Toiletries first and foremost.

But how is it possible that inside that clinic you don't know the prices of every single thing?

As if I worked in a store and didn't know the prices of the products I sell?

I worked as a secretary, and I understand that a secretary must also know the prices of every single service.

If I wanted to pay in cash, and I have the exact prices, but I really have to be inconvenienced. Forgive the term, because you don't know the actual prices, but we're kidding, but I don't think you've only been working there for a day.

I should report you to the finance department for this.
